data.title: Lentigo — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lentigo** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. Define lentigo.**
- Small, well-circumscribed, uniformly brown-black macule (1–5 mm, solar types larger) due to increased number of melanocytes along the basal layer with elongated pigmented rete ridges; does not fade in winter

**Q2. Discuss the various types of lentigines (PYQ).**
- Lentigo simplex: childhood, any site including mucosa/palms, not sun-related
- Solar (senile/actinic) lentigo — 'age spots/liver spots': middle-aged/elderly, sun-exposed dorsa of hands, face; PUVA lentigines (after PUVA — larger, darker, atypical), sunburn (ink-spot) lentigo — reticulate black ('ink-spot') after sunburn
- Mucosal (labial/genital) melanotic macules/lentigines
- Agminated (segmental cluster)
- Lentigo maligna — melanoma in situ on chronically sun-damaged face of elderly (not a true lentigo)
- Syndromic lentiginoses: Peutz–Jeghers (perioral, lips, buccal mucosa, digits; GI hamartomatous polyps, cancer risk — STK11), LEOPARD/Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (PTPN11; Lentigines, ECG abnormalities, Ocular hypertelorism, Pulmonary stenosis, Abnormal genitalia, Retarded growth, Deafness), Carney complex (LAMB/NAME — lentigines, atrial myxomas, blue naevi, endocrine overactivity, PRKAR1A), Laugier–Hunziker (oral/lip lentigines + longitudinal melanonychia, benign), Cowden, Bannayan–Riley–Ruvalcaba (penile lentigines, PTEN), centrofacial lentiginosis (Touraine), inherited patterned lentiginosis (black skin), xeroderma pigmentosum

**Q3. Histopathology of solar lentigo.**
- Elongated club-shaped/budding rete ridges with heavy basal pigmentation and slightly increased melanocytes, solar elastosis, no nests (vs junctional naevus)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Freckle, junctional naevus (nests), seborrhoeic keratosis (flat — reticulated SK), pigmented actinic keratosis, lentigo maligna (asymmetric, variegated, irregular border, dermoscopy — annular granular, asymmetric follicular openings, rhomboid structures), lichen planus-like keratosis, café-au-lait macule

**Q5. Dermoscopy.**
- Solar lentigo: light-brown fingerprint-like or reticular pattern, moth-eaten sharp border, homogeneous structureless areas; mucosal: parallel/ring-like patterns

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Benign — photoprotection
- Cryotherapy, Q-switched (532/755 nm) or picosecond lasers, IPL, chemical peels (TCA, glycolic), topical retinoids, hydroquinone/triple cream, thiamidol
- Biopsy any atypical lesion before destructive treatment (to exclude lentigo maligna)
- Syndromic: screening for associated systemic disease (Peutz–Jeghers — endoscopy; Carney — echocardiography)

## Quick spotter facts
- Perioral and buccal lentigines + GI polyps — Peutz–Jeghers (STK11)
- Lentigines + myxomas + endocrine overactivity — Carney complex
- Biopsy atypical facial 'lentigo' in elderly — lentigo maligna

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Lentigines). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
